title: Sections transport for a specified completed coefficient-model map
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $R=\mathcal O_E$, $S=\mathcal O_L$ and $B_F=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,s}$ for $F=E,L$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. For a bounded finite-projective complex $A$ over $R$ and $C$ over $S$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], let $\mathscr L_EA=B_E\otimes_{\underline R}\underline A$ and $\mathscr L_LC=B_L\otimes_{\underline S}\underline C$, using constant module sheaves and sheaf tensor [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Assume these models are derived-complete bounded constructible [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Use sections $\Gamma$ of [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] and their canonical units $e_A:A\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(s,\mathscr L_EA)$, $e_C:C\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(s,\mathscr L_LC)$, sending $x$ to $1\otimes x$.
Let $v:A\otimes_R S\to C$ be a cochain map, and let $g:\mathscr L_EA\otimes_{B_E}^L B_L\to\mathscr L_LC$ be its coefficient-sheaf realization, characterized on local generators by $g((b\otimes x)\otimes b')=bb'\,\underline{v(x\otimes1)}$. Let $\chi$ be the specified completion comparison [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], $T_{L/E}$ the strict-tower functor [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], and $\varphi$ the specified sections comparison [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. In $D(S)$ one has the actual equality
$$e_C^{-1}\Gamma(s,g\chi^{-1})\varphi_{L/E,\mathscr L_EA}^{-1}(e_A\otimes1)=v.$$
Equivalently, using the canonical sections-tensor map $\theta$, $\varphi^{-1}=\Gamma(s,\chi)\theta$ and the left side evaluates on $x\otimes a$ as $v(x\otimes a)$. The equality is natural for derived maps between these perfect models and respects the identity normalization for $L=E$ and the specified integral and module associators for $E\subset L\subset M$.
Tensoring this equality over $S$ with $L$ gives the corresponding equality of rationalized comparisons. More generally, if such maps $v,g$ are components of natural comparisons between $R$-linear functors, either covariant or contravariant, then the same comparison is natural for morphisms of the raw scalar-localized source category [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization, def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Explicitly every such morphism is $u/\varpi_E^n$ after a common denominator is chosen; each localized functor sends it to its value on $u$ divided by $\varpi_E^n$, with precomposition for a contravariant functor. The naturality equations are independent of the fraction representative and hold also on these morphisms. Identity and tower equations remain valid after this localization.

proof.text: Fix the actual units by their formula x ↦ 1 tensor x. At the final object of the pro-etale site of the algebraically closed point, sheafification of a concrete presheaf is bijective on sections by [lem-trf-point-sheafification-final]. Apply this first to the constant module presheaf. Constant-ring sections identify with the original coefficient ring, and completed-ring sections do too, by the existing coefficient normalization in [lem-weil-point-finite-free-sections-tensor]. The constant-to-completion map intertwines these two ring equivalences. Consequently the existing tensor-square isomorphism, with the identity coefficient homomorphism, identifies the module with sections of the scalar-extension presheaf. Apply final-object sheafification once more (the constant-section ring equivalence and final sheafification isomorphism of [lem-trf-point-finite-reduction-section-algebra]), then the object equality prescribed by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The composite is a module isomorphism whose value at x is exactly the recorded generator 1 tensor x, including both sheafification units and the prescribed object transport. This argument works for any coefficient module; no projective splitting is needed. Naturality of constant sheafification and of the normalized ordinary change-of-rings witness gives b tensor x ↦ b tensor f(x). Thus these component isomorphisms commute with differentials and assemble to a chain isomorphism. Equality on every element in every degree proves uniqueness. This proves unit_existsUnique and gives naturality of the selected unit and its derived counterpart.

proof.text: Put $K=\mathscr L_EA$. Apply [lem-weil-point-derived-sections-tensor-descent] with this $K$: ordinary sheaf extension by $B_L$ computes derived extension, and $\theta^D$ is the derived class of the termwise sections-tensor map. Its formula is $n\otimes a\mapsto n\otimes a_s$, where $a_s$ is the constant-value section. Sections preserve quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. These facts justify using the displayed cochain representatives for $\Gamma(g)$ and $\theta$, without assuming a sectionwise description of an arbitrary sheaf tensor product. This use of $\theta$ applies to every derived morphism, as the cited descent statement explicitly asserts. The Lean helper sectionsTensor_counit_factor expands the specified derived theta and uses the ordinary derived comparison normalization. After cancellation of the comparison and its inverse, exact-functor composition and natural-isomorphism factorization identities give exactly the localized termwise theta, with the actual completed scalar counit.

proof.text:
Completeness and bounded constructibility of $K$ are hypotheses of the item, so [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] supplies the specified invertible $\chi_K$. By the defining equation in [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension], $\varphi_K^{-1}=\Gamma(\chi_K)\theta_K$. Functoriality of sections and cancellation of this very $\chi_K$ give
$$e_C^{-1}\Gamma(g\chi_K^{-1})\varphi_K^{-1}(e_A\otimes1)
=e_C^{-1}\Gamma(g)\Gamma(\chi_K^{-1})\Gamma(\chi_K)\theta_K(e_A\otimes1)
=e_C^{-1}\Gamma(g)\theta_K(e_A\otimes1).$$
All compositions are in $D(S)$. In particular there is no assertion that an arbitrary isomorphism with the completed tower has this cancellation property.

proof.text:
For $x\in A^i$ and $a\in S$, the last composite before $e_C^{-1}$ in Step 3 sends
$$x\otimes a\longmapsto(1\otimes x)\otimes a_s
\longmapsto a_s\,\underline{v(x\otimes1)}
=1\otimes v(x\otimes a)=e_C(v(x\otimes a)).$$
The first arrow is the pure-tensor formula of [lem-weil-point-finite-free-sections-tensor]; the second is precisely the assumed local-generator formula for $g$, with $b=1$ and $b'=a_s$. The middle equality is balancing in the sheaf tensor and $S$-linearity of $v$. Pure tensors generate $A^i\otimes_R S$, so the two maps agree in every degree. All maps have degree zero, and the differentials agree by the cochain-map condition on $v$. We obtain equality of chain maps, hence the asserted actual equality in $D(S)$, not merely equality on cohomology. The implemented cochain equality first cancels e_C on the right. Degreewise ModuleCat.ExtendScalars.hom_ext reduces the equality of O_L-linear maps to the tensors 1 tensor x. The chosen unit specifications, pointSectionsTensor_existsUnique, and Realizes at b=b′=1 identify these generators. The pure-tensor clause follows by rewriting this actual cochain equality; the displayed cancellation identity is the defining equation of phi. In transport_eq, naturality of the exact sections factorization moves the localized sheaf map past its factorization isomorphism. sectionsTensor_counit_factor then identifies the result with the image under Q of chainTransport, preceded by the prescribed module-tensor factorization. Substitution of chainTransport_spec gives moduleMap exactly.

proof.text: For chain maps $p:A'\to A$ over $R$ and $q:C\to C'$ over $S$, the realization of $qv(p\otimes1)$ agrees with the corresponding composite of realized maps: both send $((b\otimes x)\otimes b')$ to $bb'\,\underline{qv(p(x)\otimes1)}$. Step 1 gives naturality of the units. The sections-tensor comparison is natural for arbitrary derived maps by [lem-weil-point-derived-sections-tensor-descent], and $\varphi$ is natural by [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. To pass from chain maps to all maps between perfect module models, use [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative]: these bounded projective complexes represent derived maps by chain maps uniquely up to chain homotopy. Realization, sections, and scalar tensor preserve the equation $p-p'=dh+hd$ termwise. Thus their values and the equality of Step 4 are independent of the representative and natural for every such derived map, in both variables. In the implementation, transport_formula expands phi inverse and cancels chi followed by chi inverse. The unit equations supplied by derivedMap_existsUnique and naturality of the existing theta natural isomorphism then prove transport_naturality on arbitrary derived arrows. Rational transport is beta inverse followed by rationalization of integral transport, by beta naturality. For derivedMap_existsUnique, the upper bound and projectivity in IsModel make the source K-projective. The existing representative theorem supplies a chain map. Injectivity of Qh on maps from that source, conjugated by the quotient-to-derived factorization isomorphism, implies that any two representatives of the same derived arrow are chain homotopic. The additive realization maps this homotopy to a homotopy, so its two localized maps agree. This proves uniqueness of the realized derived arrow without choosing any additional data. Naturality of the actual normalized unit, followed by naturality of the exact-sections factorization, proves its required derived sections square.

proof.text: For $L=E$, use multiplication on both tensors. Then $\theta(n\otimes a)=an$, and [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] normalizes $\varphi$ to the identity after the specified completeness identification. Hence the formula of Step 4 retains $v$ with no extra unit automorphism. For $E\subset L\subset M$, write $T=\mathcal O_M$ and choose a further model map $w:C\otimes_S T\to D$. The ordinary associators and sections maps are compatible by [lem-weil-point-derived-tensor-tower-coherence]. Their common tensor formula is $((n\otimes a)\otimes b)\mapsto n\otimes ab$. For the model maps, the iterated realization sends $((x\otimes a)\otimes b)$ to $w(v(x\otimes a)\otimes b)$; the realization of $w(v\otimes1)$ after the module associator has exactly the same value. The integral associator is the ordinary one conjugated by $\chi$, and the displayed tower equation of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] identifies its sections with this module associator. Substituting $\varphi^{-1}=\Gamma(\chi)\theta$ cancels each adjacent $\chi^{-1}\chi$, just as in Step 3. This proves the tower compatibility for the specified completed comparisons. The Lean proof transport_identity substitutes the derived sections unit square into transport_formula; naturality of the module unit cancels the two model-unit factors. For transport_tower, invert the integral sections tower equality as an equality of isomorphisms. Apply inverse-comparison naturality to the actual map chi inverse followed by g. Naturality of the module associator and cancellation of the intermediate model units give the stated integral tower equation.

proof.text: Apply $-\otimes_S L$ to the equality of Step 4. This is a functor on derived module categories by [lem-weil-coefficient-complex-rationalization], so it preserves the equality and both inverse equations of the unit comparisons. Identify its source with $(A\otimes_R E)\otimes_E L$ through the specified $\beta$, whose formula is $((x\otimes a)\otimes b)\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes ab$. The transported rational map is therefore exactly $v\otimes_S L$. Naturality and the identity and tower equations persist: the same cited statement asserts these properties for $\beta$, and [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] asserts them for the rationalized sections comparisons. Equivalently their common coefficient calculation multiplies all factors in the final field. The rational identity follows from rationalTransport_formula and the existing beta unit law. For the rational tower, invert the beta tower equality as an equality of isomorphisms, then use beta inverse naturality at the actual first integral transport. This proves the specified field-associator equation. No further named obligation is introduced.

proof.text: For the more general natural-comparison clause, put $t=\varpi_E$. By [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization] the objects of the raw localized source are unchanged and a Hom module is $H\otimes_R R[1/t]$. The isomorphism in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-tensor] identifies it with the fractions of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Explicitly, a finite sum $\sum_i u_i\otimes(r_i/t^{n_i})$ is $u/t^N$, where $N=\max_i n_i$ and $u=\sum_i r_i t^{N-n_i}u_i$ (the empty sum is $0/1$). Equality $u/t^n=u'/t^m$ means $t^k(t^m u-t^n u')=0$ for some $k$. For either integral linear functor $F$, applying $F$ gives the same equation in its target Hom module. In the rational target $t$ is invertible, so multiplication by $t^{-k-m-n}$ gives $t^{-n}F(u)=t^{-m}F(u')$. Hence the fraction formula is well defined even when the integral Hom modules have $t$-torsion. For the implemented common denominator, use Mathlib IsLocalization.tensorProduct_isLocalizedModule and IsLocalizedModule.surj for the tensor-with-one map. Surjectivity supplies t^n times f = 1 tensor a. Multiplication by invSelf(t)^n gives f = invSelf(t)^n tensor a, valid also with t-torsion and in the zero localization.

Let $\eta:F\Rightarrow G$ be the integral comparison whose components are the maps in the question, after the unit identifications already proved. Apply [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization] to extend the two linear functors and this comparison to the raw scalar-localized categories; here the coefficient map is the given inclusion into the rational target and sends $t$ to a unit. For $u:X\to Y$, covariant naturality reads $G(u)\eta_X=\eta_YF(u)$; multiplying by $t^{-n}$ gives $\bar G(u/t^n)\bar\eta_X=\bar\eta_Y\bar F(u/t^n)$. For contravariant functors apply the same cited lemma to the opposite source category, whose Hom modules and reversed composition are still $R$-linear. In ordinary notation its equation is $G(u)\eta_Y=\eta_XF(u)$, and division gives $\bar G(u/t^n)\bar\eta_Y=\bar\eta_X\bar F(u/t^n)$. This is precomposition in the contravariant argument. Step 8 proves that both displayed fraction equations are independent of the chosen numerator and denominator. The Lean proof uses extension_spec for the two fraction formulas and extensionNatTrans_naturality for the displayed equation on every raw morphism. Applying each extension functor to an equality of raw fractions and rewriting its fraction formula proves representative independence directly. The contravariant theorem specializes this same assertion to I opposite and takes the unop of the numerator.

proof.text: Finally the localization functors preserve identities and composition, and the extension lemma preserves vertical composition and whiskering [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization]. Therefore applying localization to each side of the integral identity and tower equations of Step 6 gives the corresponding equation on the same objects in the raw localized categories. Step 9 supplies naturality on all their arrows, so these componentwise equations are equations of the localized natural comparisons. No additional objects or idempotent summands enter: [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] specifies the raw scalar localization. This proves the final identity and tower assertions as well as the general localized-naturality assertion. In scalarLocalizedCoherence, evaluate the given integral transformation equality at X and apply the localization functor, rewriting its map_comp equation. Apply extensionNatTrans_naturality to the actual composite a followed by c; substitute the localized integral square at the source. The finite-subfield theorem specializes transport_eq after converting both intrinsic constructibility hypotheses with pointIntegralConstructible_iff.
